root_cause.text: In `spi_register_controller()`, the error path for `spi_alloc_pcpu_stats()` failure did not call `device_del(&ctlr->dev)` after the controller had already been registered with driver core, leaving a stale registered device that could access freed controller/driver resources.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a shared `del_ctrl:` label with `device_del(&ctlr->dev)` for later registration failures and changes the queue-init failure path to jump there; the CVE/commit message explicitly says per-cpu statistics allocation failure during controller registration must also deregister from driver core to avoid “use-after-free (of driver resources) and unclocked register accesses.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the common del_ctrl error path when queue initialization fails so controller registration cleanup is handled correctly.
intent_record.what: In spi_register_controller(), the error handling after spi_controller_initialize_queue(ctlr) was changed from an inline block that called device_del(&ctlr->dev) and then jumped to free_bus_id, to a single conditional jump to del_ctrl when status is nonzero.
intent_record.how: On queue initialization failure, control now follows the shared del_ctrl cleanup path instead of manually deleting the device and skipping directly to free_bus_id, ensuring the function uses centralized cleanup logic and likely avoids incomplete or inconsistent resource teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure failed SPI controller registration unregisters the device before freeing its bus ID during cleanup.
intent_record.what: A new error-handling label `del_ctrl:` was added between `destroy_queue:` and `free_bus_id:`, and `device_del(&ctlr->dev);` was inserted under that label so cleanup now explicitly removes the controller device before proceeding to bus ID removal.
intent_record.how: On error paths that jump to this new label, the registered device is now unregistered from the device model before the controller bus ID is freed, preventing a partially registered SPI controller device from being left behind during failed controller registration.

grouping_result.intent: Ensure failed SPI controller registration unregisters the device before freeing its bus ID during cleanup.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix SPI controller registration failure cleanup so partially registered controllers are properly unregistered and cleaned up through the correct error path.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly fix the registration failure cleanup path in spi_register_controller() by routing failures through proper controller/device teardown and explicitly unregistering the device before freeing related resources, matching the root cause of leaving a stale registered device after spi_alloc_pcpu_stats() or similar post-registration failures.

candidates.rationale: When spi_alloc_pcpu_stats() failed after the controller had already been registered, this jump bypassed controller/device unregistration and went straight to freeing the bus ID, leaving the registered device stale and able to reference freed resources.
This cleanup target did not perform device_del(&ctlr->dev). Routing post-registration failures here caused incomplete teardown of an already registered controller device.

vuln_statements.explanation: This error-path jump was taken when spi_alloc_pcpu_stats() failed after the controller had already been registered with the driver core. Jumping directly to free_bus_id bypassed the cleanup path that unregisters/deletes the device, causing an already-registered device to remain stale while related controller resources were freed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff provides enough of `spi_register_controller()` to evaluate the relevant error paths. The root cause is specifically that after `device_add(&ctlr->dev)` succeeds, a later failure in `spi_alloc_pcpu_stats()` should call `device_del(&ctlr->dev)` but does not. In this commit version, after successful `device_add(&ctlr->dev)`, the function may later jump to the new `free_bus_id:` label, which only does `idr_remove(&spi_master_idr, ctlr->bus_num)` and returns. The shown code still has `device_del(&ctlr->dev)` only in the queue initialization failure path: `if (status) { device_del(&ctlr->dev); goto free_bus_id; }`. There is no corresponding `device_del(&ctlr->dev)` shown for the later statistics-allocation failure path before the function reaches `of_register_spi_devices(ctlr);` / `acpi_register_spi_devices(ctlr);`. Since this commit is about freeing the bus id on error paths and the displayed logic does not add `device_del(&ctlr->dev)` to the post-`device_add()` `spi_alloc_pcpu_stats()` failure path, the vulnerable construct remains present and the fix for the stale registered device issue is not yet included.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant function body `spi_register_controller()` is shown in full, so the snippet is sufficient to inspect the error path after controller registration. The root-cause vulnerability is specifically the failure path when `spi_alloc_pcpu_stats()` fails after `device_add(&ctlr->dev)`, requiring a matching `device_del(&ctlr->dev)`. In this commit's `spi_register_controller()` there is no call to `spi_alloc_pcpu_stats()` at all, so the vulnerable construct is not present in the shown code. The post-registration error handling that does exist is for queue initialization: `status = spi_controller_initialize_queue(ctlr); if (status) { device_del(&ctlr->dev); goto done; }`, which correctly deletes the device for that failure case. Because the specific failing allocation path from the root cause is completely absent, `has_bug` must be false. And because the fix for that specific bug would be handling `spi_alloc_pcpu_stats()` failure with `device_del(&ctlr->dev)`, but neither the allocation nor that fix path exists here, `is_fixed` is false.
